facts.fact: The princes' way route-song, taught to Kunal by Pritam at twelve: 'First the turn that turns you home, / then seven breaths and none to keep, / then the stone that weeps and weeps, / step on the wet where the water sleeps.' It ends at the weeping stone; Kunal has never been taught the rest.
facts.why: needed because the beat has Kunal sing Pritam's verse through the squeeze and the meltwater step.

facts.fact: Inside the cleft: 81 paces from the mouth to the first turn (a hairpin that doubles back on the left, 'the turn that turns you home'); then 40 paces to the seven-breaths slot (cross sideways, breathe out fully and take no breath until through); then 20 paces to the weeping stone (a glazed ledge with a sheet of meltwater, third step on the wet is the bad one); then 304 paces of dry gravel passage marked by small blue cairn-stones.
facts.why: needed because the beat requires the squeeze, the meltwater step and Kunal giving every turn and count.

facts.fact: The way ends, for this trip, in a hollow wide as a hall whose floor slopes into black water; the blue cairn-stones continue under the surface. Too far to dive with half a lamp of oil and one night's bread, so the pair turn back.
facts.why: needed because the beat has them stop where the way drops toward deeper water and return for stores.

facts.fact: Kunal's furthest point was the first turn (hairpin) at age twelve; he could not see cairn-light then, but sees it now as a bound man.
facts.why: needed to square the beat's 'past his furthest point' with chapter 17's earlier fact.

facts.fact: Ila nearly tells Kunal about the queen's letter and stops, reasoning that paying early would turn his gift into a trade; she says she will tell him 'when I can pay it properly.'
facts.why: needed because the beat has her almost telling and stopping on the words 'through the mountain'.
